# Gladly API (1.0)

...

## REST API

Clients can access the REST API via HTTPS at your organization's Gladly domain (e.g. `https://{organization}.gladly.com`).

Resources follow REST semantics and utilize industry-standard HTTP verbs, response codes, and authentication schemes. In addition, all responses and payloads are in JSON with consistent error codes and formats.

## Lookup API

The Gladly Lookup API allows your organization to provide data services to power the agent's experience with a complete view of your customers' information, transactions, and activity. You can provide a web service that implements the Lookup API and Gladly will call it when that data is needed.

Like the REST API, the Lookup API is specified using REST semantics, and exchanges JSON requests and responses authenticated and signed with secure keys.

...

# Getting Started

Think of this section as getting the keys to unlocking your access to the Gladly APIs. First, you'll need to set up an account with the necessary API permissions. With these permissions, you can then go on to create the API Token(s) you need to access Gladly's API resources.

## Permissions

Gladly Administrators can set API permissions on an agent-by-agent basis. We'll discuss how this maps to API access in the section on authentication below.

To allow a user to create API tokens and access the API:

1. Log in to your Gladly instance.
2. Open the menu on the top left-hand corner of the page.
3. Navigate to Settings > *Users
4. Search and click the user profile you wish to give access to.
5. You'll see a permission called API User. Select it, while making sure to keep the user's Agent role intact.
6. Hit Save to give access.

We recommend creating a dedicated user to make API calls, whose account won't be used for agent and organization management. This will help you with any future audits of API activity vs. agent activity.

## Creating API Tokens

You must create an API token to access Gladly API resources (see above Permissions). If your profile already has access to the API User permission, you'll see a menu item titled More settings. Click More settings:

Click API Tokens, then the Create Token button on the upper right-hand corner of the page:

A token will be generated and named, by default, New Token (though depending on whether you have existing tokens, it may be named New Token 2, or New Token 3, etc.). You can rename the token to something more easily referenceable by clicking the name to edit.

This token will be associated with your agent profile, which we refer to as the API User in this document.

For security purposes, you'll only see a new token once before you navigate away from the page.

## Replacing/Rotating API Tokens

Should you lose this token, or wish to rotate your application keys, you can do the following:

1. Generate a new token.
2. Store the new token in a secure location.
3. Delete the old token.
4. Update your applications/scripts with the new token.

# Authentication

## BasicAuth

Gladly API uses token-based Basic Authentication. API tokens are associated with designated Gladly users. To create and use an API token, your user must have the API User permission. An API token can be used to perform any API request without restriction.

| user name | password |
| --- | --- |
| agent email | API token |

The credentials must be passed via an `Authorization` HTTP header. All requests must be made over HTTPS.

```shell
curl -u user@organization.com:$GLADLY_API_TOKEN \
https://organization.gladly.com/api/v1/organization
```

|  Security Scheme Type  |  HTTP  |
| --- | --- |
|  HTTP Authorization Scheme  |  basic  |

...

# Public Answer

A Public Answer in Gladly represents a consumer-facing Answer.

The Public Answers API allows you to search and retrieve Public Answers (created directly in the Gladly UI), which you can display in the Chat web widget, use to build your website's help center/FAQ page, or publish on any page on your website.

This API can be used without an API token because it only provides access to public content. You may also work with Gladly Support to enable CORS access so the API can be used directly from client-side javascript.

# Generate API Tokens and Create Webhooks

| **REQUIRED USER ROLE** API User | **PERMISSION OVERVIEW** View permissions by role |
| --- | --- |

API tokens are required to use Gladly APIs for security and authentication purposes. Tokens can be accessed and created by users who at least have an API user role.

## Before you start

- For integrations not built by Gladly, a Gladly Administrator should create a new user with an API role + Agent and/or Administrator (check with your integration partner to confirm the required roles) account for *each* integration. This account should be used to access Gladly to create the API tokens or webhooks.
  - The integration partner should provide the email address to be used with the integration's user account in Gladly. They must also access emails from this account to activate their Gladly account to create API tokens or webhooks.
- API tokens are tied to a single user account and a particular environment. For example, an API token attached to Gladly user *developer@customer.com* in the Sandbox environment is not valid for *developer@customer.com* in the Production environment.
  - We recommend creating a dedicated Gladly user to make API calls whose account won't be used for Agent and organization management. This will help you with any future audits of API activity vs. Agent activity.

## Create a unique user account linked to webhooks or tokens

1. As an Administrator, create a user to use explicitly to create and attach webhooks or tokens.
  - Be sure to add the user with at least an API User role + Agent and/or Administrator. If this user needs access to reports, they'll need Administrator access. For a complete list of user permissions, click here.
  - **Note –** We recommend creating a dedicated user to make API calls.
    - Use the email address provided by the integration partner if you're given one.
  - Use a name to help you quickly identify the integration user. For example, "Retale Integration."
2. An email will be sent to the user. Someone must complete the registration and sign in to Gladly to create API tokens or webhooks. They'll have 24 hours to accept the user invitation before it expires.
  - See How do I reset my password for login issues.
  - For SSO users, see Manager Users through SSO for more information.

> [!CAUTION]
> Deactivating an API User
> 
> If a user account with API tokens or webhooks attached to it is deactivated, apps or external sources using the token or webhook linked to the user will stop working.

2. Click **Settings**.
3. Under the **App Developer Tools** category, click **API tokens**. The API tokens page will show you a list of currently available API tokens.

- Click the token name (e.g., Token 1) to rename the token to make it easy to identify how the token is used.

Create up to 50 webhooks for your organization. See our developer guide for more information about webhooks.

2. Click **Settings**.
3. Under the **App Developer Tools** category, click **Webhooks**. The Webhooks page will show you a list of webhooks you currently have configured.
4. Click **Create Webhook**.

  - **Name –** Enter a name to help you identify the app using a webhook.

  - **Username (Optional) –** Enter the username for the app you are integrating.

# Authentication

## Basic Authentication

Perhaps the most familiar authentication option, basic auth (as it is often called) requires an Agent to provide a username and password for a request. This is most common with custom integrations.

## Custom Headers

This form of authentication provides an option for additional information. For example, this can be set up to use when specific information is needed in addition to defaults, particularly with troubleshooting.

## Request Signing

This process can be more complex, so we have dedicated an in-depth section to it here.

## Generate Gladly API token

Next, login to Gladly as a user with API User permission and generate an API token for your user.

## Make an API Request

1. Open your Postman Desktop application.
2. Click on the + icon to create a new tab.
3. Click on the Authorization tab.
4. Select **Basic** as the Authorization Type.
5. Enter your username (your Gladly login email) and Password (the Gladly API token you just generated).
6. Select your HTTP request method (e.g., for GET Organziations this is GET).
7. Enter your HTTP request URL (e.g., https://organization.gladly.com/api/v1/organization).ccc.ccc)
8. If you are making a PATCH or POST request, remember to set the payload body by clicking on the Body tab and then selecting `raw` and `JSON`.
9. Click **Send**. You'll then see an API response body and status below your request.

# Configure an App

## Configuring an app

> [!CAUTION]
> Secure API Tokens
> 
> - Do not store API Token information directly in App Platform files, or pass token information from one function to another (e.g., short-lived tokens).
> - Do not pass API Token information or elicit for that information via Guides.
> 
> See Non-Oauth apps to learn how how external app secrets should be uploaded via the appcfg CLI and how to register an OAUTH App.

## Glossary

As you will run below commands, it will be important to understand the following terms and how they will be used.

`application identifier` - e.g. gladly.com/shopify/v2.0.7

`--name` - this shows up in the UI and should have a helpful name. For example “Shopify Dev Store v3.0.4”. This name informs: what app it is, to which instance of the app the configuration connects to, which version of the app it is.

`--activate` - set this to true if you wish to immediately enable this configuration to begin servicing requests

## Configure your app

#### Non-Oauth apps

```bash
appcfg apps config create <application identifier> \
--name "My Configuration" \
--config '{"non-secret":"configuration", "host":"www.example.com"}' \
--secrets '{"a-secret":"api-token"}' \
--activate
```

> [!NOTE]
> Tip
> 
> The `—config` flag is required even if the configuration is empty

Now an instance of the external app has been associated with the required configuration (such as API token stored on the configuration), and is officially ready for use. You can verify this by running the `appcfg apps config list` command:

...

|     APP

...

### Oauth

> [!WARNING]
> Registering your Oauth domain
> 
> Make sure that have contacted Gladly Support to register your Oauth domain before running the command below

1. #### Create configuration

```bash
appcfg apps config create <application identifier> /
--name "My Configuration" /
--config '{"non-secret":"configuration"}'
--secrets '{}'
```
2. #### Authorize

```plaintext
appcfg apps oauth "My Configuration"
```

> [!NOTE]
> Autocomplete
> 
> With autocomplete, hit Tab after `appcfg apps config create`, and it will pull up all installed apps that are ready for configuration. The list will filter on partial matches, i.e. typing the identifier partially:
>

...

> gladly.com/big_commerce/v1.0.3          gladly.com/big_commerce/v2.0.0          gladly.com/developer/v1.0.0             gladly.com/install-test-epsilon/v1.2.4  gladly.com/shopify/v2.0.7

# Setup and Testing

Congratulations on building your Gladly integration. Now, you can test the myriad possibilities of the Gladly API in a safe, secure space. This guide will help you understand the testing and iteration process.

## Sandbox environment

Your sandbox environment will be accessible via the URL below where `organization` is your company name.

```plaintext
https://{organization}.gladly.qa
```

# Overview

You can integrate easily with Gladly by calling Gladly's REST API and implementing the Lookup API to provide data from your own services.

Some examples of what you do through Gladly APIs include managing customer profile data, interacting with a customer's timeline, providing the latest information about a customer's orders, and more.

## REST API

Clients can access the REST API via HTTPS at your organization's Gladly domain (e.g. `https://{organization}.gladly.com`).

Resources follow REST semantics and utilize industry-standard HTTP verbs, response codes, and authentication schemes. In addition, all responses and payloads are in JSON with consistent error codes and formats.

## Lookup API

The Gladly Lookup API allows your organization to provide data services to power the agent's experience with a complete view of your customers' information, transactions, and activity. You can provide a web service that implements the Lookup API and Gladly will call it when that data is needed.

Like the REST API, the Lookup API is specified using REST semantics, and exchanges JSON requests and responses authenticated and signed with secure keys.

Gladly will perform lookups when certain activities occur within Gladly, such as when a customer's profile is loaded.

A detailed overview of Lookup Adaptor architecture, requests, resposnes and more can be found here.

## Testing

Test the myriad possibilities of the Gladly API in a safe, secure space. We'll enable the Gladly API in a separate sandbox environment, so you can experiment freely without impacting your production environment (or vice versa).

Your sandbox environment is accessible at `https://{organization}.gladly.qa`, where `organization` is your company name. For specific API endpoints, see documentation below.

# Getting Started

Think of this section as getting the keys to unlocking your access to the Gladly APIs. First, you'll need to set up an account with the necessary API permissions. With these permissions, you can then go on to create the API Token(s) you need to access Gladly's API resources.

## Permissions

Gladly Administrators can set API permissions on an agent-by-agent basis. We'll discuss how this maps to API access in the section on authentication below.

To allow a user to create API tokens and access the API:

1. Log in to your Gladly instance.
2. Open the menu on the top left-hand corner of the page.
3. Navigate to Settings > *Users
4. Search and click the user profile you wish to give access to.
5. You'll see a permission called API User. Select it, while making sure to keep the user's Agent role intact.
6. Hit Save to give access.

We recommend creating a dedicated user to make API calls, whose account won't be used for agent and organization management. This will help you with any future audits of API activity vs. agent activity.

## Creating API Tokens

You must create an API token to access Gladly API resources (see above Permissions). If your profile already has access to the API User permission, you'll see a menu item titled More settings. Click More settings:

This token will be associated with your agent profile, which we refer to as the API User in this document.

For security purposes, you'll only see a new token once before you navigate away from the page.

2. Store the new token in a secure location.

# Gladly

> Integration details and setup guide for the Gladly connector in Alloy Automation.

...

## Set Up Guide

### Trial Access

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Offers free trial? | Gladly typically requires a demo and custom pricing. Request a demo and trial access at https://www.gladly.com/request-demo. |
| Requires requires paid sandbox | Contact Gladly for sandbox or trial environment access. |
| Requires partnership to obtain authentication? | No. Once you have a Gladly account, API credentials can be obtained from your account settings. |

---

### Authentication (HTTP Basic Authentication)

Gladly uses HTTP Basic Authentication with your Agent Email and API Token.

1. Log in to your Gladly account at https://{subdomain}.gladly.com.
2. Navigate to Settings → Developers or API Settings (admin access required).
3. Generate or copy your API Token.
4. Enter your Agent Email as the username and API Token as the password in Alloy Automation.
5. Also configure your Gladly subdomain in the connection settings.

#### API Documentation

For detailed API documentation, visit: https://developer.gladly.com/

#### Important Notes

# Set up the Gladly MCP for Claude

Connect Claude to your Gladly organization so you can investigate sessions, improve Guides and Workflows, and test changes in plain English. Setup takes about 5 minutes and doesn't require any downloads. To learn what the Gladly MCP for Claude does, see What is the Gladly MCP for Claude?

## Before you begin

Make sure all of the following are true:

- Gladly has enabled MCP access for your organization. If you're not sure, ask your Gladly account team.
- You have an eligible role in Gladly: Team Manager, Compliance Admin, or Admin, or a custom role with the Manage Gladly AI, View Gladly AI, or Review Gladly AI permission. Other roles can't connect.

- You know the address you use to sign in to Gladly, for example `acme.us-1.gladly.com`.

## Add the Gladly plugin

The Gladly plugin adds the `/gladly-setup` command, which builds your personal connector address and checks your connection. The connector you add next is what gives Claude access to Gladly.

1. ... Look for **Plugins** in the sidebar or in Settings.
2. Add a marketplace and enter the Gladly marketplace address:

```plaintext

```

...

## Get your connector address

1. In a new chat, type `/gladly-setup`, or ask Claude to "set up Gladly."
2. Enter the address you use to sign in to Gladly. Claude builds your personal connector address.

| You enter | Claude gives you |

| `acme.us-1.gladly.com` | `https://mcp.us-1.gladly.com/acme/mcp` |

If you sign in on an older address without the region, such as acme.gladly.com, enter that instead. Both work.

...

3. Keep the settings Claude detects.

...

4. Select **Connect**. Gladly opens in your browser. Sign in if you're asked.
5. Review what Claude is asking to do, then select **Allow access**.

# What are MCP connections?

An **MCP connection** links Gladly AI to an external system so it can look up information or take action during a Customer Conversation. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI systems discover and call the tools an external system offers. With an MCP connection, Gladly AI can check an order status, search a product catalog, or look up store hours while it helps a customer, using live data from your own systems.

![](https://cdn.us.document360.io/7047b671-c4f2-4df0-bb0a-b9b511fd2452/Images/Documentation/mcp exchange.png?sv=2026-02-06&spr=https&st=2026-11-23T10%3A48%3A29Z&se=2026-11-23T11%3A48%3A29Z&sr=b&sp=r&sig=tCodohOxjhGyCS%2Fs2uxNND6Xo9kJanXH4XzL6oJEAgk%3D)

Instead of building a custom App Platform integration for every external system, you register an MCP server once. Gladly discovers the tools on that server automatically.

---

## How MCP connections work

When a customer asks a question, Gladly AI decides whether one of your MCP tools can help. If it can, Gladly AI calls the tool on your MCP server, reads the response, and uses it to answer the customer.

For example, a customer asks, "Where is my order RT-1001?" Gladly AI calls an order lookup tool on your server, gets back the status, carrier, and tracking number, and shares them in its reply.

![](https://cdn.us.document360.io/7047b671-c4f2-4df0-bb0a-b9b511fd2452/Images/Documentation/connect gladly ai to mcp.png?sv=2026-02-06&spr=https&st=2026-11-23T10%3A48%3A29Z&se=2026-11-23T11%3A48%3A29Z&sr=b&sp=r&sig=%2FbR9sJdXu4fIKhCVeDOuovKWf76aUr%2F%2B4aBP89coIdg%3D)

### Servers, connections, and tools

Three terms describe how MCP fits together in Gladly:

- **Server:** The external system that offers tools, identified by its URL. For example, an MCP server for your order management system.
- **Connection:** How your org connects to a server. A connection has a name, the authentication details for the server, and an active or inactive status. You can create more than one connection to the same server, for example to use different credentials.
- **Tool:** A single capability the server offers, such as `lookup_order_status` or `search_products`. Each tool has a description and the inputs it needs.

## Where Gladly AI uses MCP tools

MCP tools reach Gladly AI only after you add them to a Guide or Skill. Adding a connection on its own doesn't change how Gladly AI responds.

In a Guide, you wrap an MCP tool in a Custom Action, then add that Action to a Guide section. The Custom Action calls the MCP tool as one of its steps, and you control what the Action collects from the customer and what it passes to the tool. MCP tools work alongside your other Actions, so a single Guide can use both.

See Set up MCP connections for the steps.

## Authentication options

Gladly supports the following authentication types for an MCP server:

- **None**
- **Bearer Token**
- **API Key**
- **OAuth (Authorization Code)**
- **OAuth (Client Credentials)**

Use the type your server requires. If you're not sure which one to use, ask the team that manages the server.

## Manage MCP connections

You manage connections from **Settings**, under **App Developer Tools**, on the **MCP** page. From there you can:

- Add a connection to a new or existing server.
- Test a connection to confirm Gladly can reach the server and find its tools.
- Run a tool on its own to see what it returns.
- View tool call logs to see each request and response.
- Edit, deactivate, or delete a connection.

...

See Set up MCP connections for step-by-step instructions.

---

> [!TIP]
> Things to know
> 
> - **Guardrails still apply.** Replies that use MCP tool data pass the same reply guardrails as any other Gladly AI reply. Gladly doesn't screen the tool's output itself, so make sure your server returns only information you're comfortable sharing with customers.
> - **Tools only.** MCP connections support tools. Resources and prompts offered by an MCP server aren't available.
> - **If a server is unreachable.** Gladly drops only that server's tools for that turn, and the rest of the conversation continues.
> - **Everything is logged.** Each tool call, including test runs, appears in the connection's tool call logs. Tool calls also appear in conversation history and action logs.

This is a Model Context Protocol endpoint — meant to be connected from an AI client, not opened in a browser. An `invalid_token` response at the URL is the auth gate working as designed; clients authenticate automatically.

# Review security and data for the Gladly MCP for Claude

Learn what Claude can see and do when it's connected to your Gladly organization, how Customer data can show up in Claude, and how to keep that data safe. To learn what the Gladly MCP for Claude does, see What is the Gladly MCP for Claude?

## How access works

- **MCP is on for your whole organization.** MCP is turned on for your organization as a whole. You can't allow or block one specific person.
- **Claude has the same access as your Gladly role.** Claude acts as you. It can see and change only what your role can in Gladly.
- **Claude signs in as you.** Each person connects with their own Gladly sign-in. There are no shared keys or API tokens.

### Roles that can connect

These roles can connect Claude to Gladly:

- Team Manager
- Compliance Admin
- Admin

A custom role can also connect if it has one of these permissions:

- Manage Gladly AI
- View Gladly AI
- Review Gladly AI

## How customer data can show up in Claude

AI sessions can include personal information, such as names, emails, and order details. Customer data can show up in Claude in two ways.

**Indirectly: pulled in to answer a question** Claude may read transcripts that include customer details to explain what happened. For example, you might ask, "Why did these returns sessions hand off to a person?"

**Directly: asked for by name** Claude can look up and show customer details that your role can see. For example, you might ask, "What was the customer's email in the session from earlier?"

**Where that data goes** Anything Claude reads becomes part of your Claude chat. From there, it's handled under your company's agreement with Anthropic and your Claude settings, such as chat history and retention. Connect Gladly only to a Claude plan your company has approved.

## Keep customer data safe

- **Limit eligible roles.** Give eligible roles only to people you trust with customer data and your AI setup.
- **Ask for patterns and summaries.** Ask for patterns and summaries instead of individual customer details, unless you need them.
- **Keep customer details out of shared spaces.** Don't copy customer details from Claude into shared docs, tickets, or channels.
- **Take care when sharing chats.** Be careful sharing Claude chats, and delete the ones you don't need, according to your data policy.
- **Check the Changelog.** Changes made through Claude show your name with "(MCP)."
- **Disconnect when needed.** To disconnect yourself, remove the connector in Claude. A Gladly administrator can remove your organization's access to MCP.

## Built-in safeguards

- **Teammate changes are protected.** If someone else changes a Gladly Agent while Claude is working, Claude's save is rejected and Claude redoes its change on the latest version. It doesn't overwrite a teammate's work.
- **Action edits are checked.** Before Claude saves an Action edit, it checks what uses the Action and stops if the change would break a Workflow step or Guide rule.
- **Changes are tracked.** Every change Claude saves appears in the Changelog under your name, tagged "(MCP)."

highlights:
# Gladly MCP server

Gladly in any MCP client, through Memtro: Gladly does not publish this server. Memtro's Gladly connector reads Gladly through its API with the credentials you connect, and one endpoint hands those tools, every other system you connect and Memtro's memory tools to Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop or anything else that speaks Streamable HTTP, as you.

## What the model can do

Gladly (customer service): customers found by email, phone or external id, their conversations with status, inbox, assignee and topics, each conversation's timeline (internal notes in full; customer messages as type and time only), tasks with comments, and the agents, inboxes, teams, topics and help-centre answers; can add internal notes, assign, close or reopen conversations, add or remove topics, create and update tasks, reply to a customer's message, send an email or SMS to a customer, create, update or delete customer profiles, and redact a message.

### Reads

- `gladly_find_customers` Find Gladly customers by exactly one of email, phone number (E.164, +14155550123) or external customer id; at most 50, most recently updated first.
- `gladly_get_customer` One Gladly customer by id: name, emails, when created and updated.
- `gladly_list_conversations` A Gladly customer's conversations, oldest first (at most 100): id, status (OPEN, WAITING, CLOSED), inbox, assigned agent, topic ids…
- `gladly_get_conversation` One Gladly conversation and its timeline, oldest first: each item's type (email, chat, SMS, call, note, task, status or topic change)…
- `gladly_list_tasks` A Gladly customer's tasks, newest first: text, status, due time, assigned inbox and agent, topics.
- `gladly_get_task` One Gladly task with its comments (agent id, text, when), oldest first.
- `gladly_list_directory` Gladly reference lists that ids point to: agents (id and name), inboxes (id, name, disabled), teams (name, description, agent ids), topics (name…

### Acts, when you ask

These change something in Gladly. The model is told to use them only when you ask for exactly that, and each one is granted by name: per team on a shared connection, by the owner on a personal one.

- `gladly_add_note` Adds an internal note to a Gladly conversation, visible to agents only; the customer is not notified.

...

Is this an official Gladly MCP server?

No. It is Memtro's MCP server with Memtro's Gladly connector behind it: the connector reads Gladly through its API with the credentials you connect on Dashboard → Connections, and Gladly publishes nothing here. The same endpoint carries every other system you connect and Memtro's memory tools.
